title: Flat buyer can afford the mortgage but cannot tell what service charges and major works will do next
job: Understand future building costs and legal rights before buying, budgeting or challenging.
trigger: Purchase pack, service-charge accounts or major-works notice arrives.
surfaceComplaint: I own the flat, but I cannot predict or understand what the building is going to charge me.
mechanism: Leasehold combines contract terms, building costs, reserve funds, consultation rights and changing regulation. Users must separate legal challengeability from financial attractiveness.

workflow.friction: history does not fully reveal future works
legal test differs from financial risk

actors.incentive: predict costs and challenge unfair charges

economics.painCostNote: Unexpected major works or service-charge escalation can affect affordability and resale.

buyer.roiLogic: Small relative to major-works exposure and purchase value.

competitors.gap: may not provide forward-looking financial scenario view

experiment.success: 6/15 pay £299+ and half uncover a material assumption/question
experiment.kill: solicitors already provide this depth or users will not pay separately

claims.text: UK reforms explicitly target service-charge transparency and access to information.
Government says leaseholders struggle to understand charges and access building information.
Separating legal challengeability from financial attractiveness is a useful product distinction.
